title: Ingredient line parser
lead: Turn a free-text ingredient line into quantity, unit, item text, notes and flags, with a confidence score (ADR 0007, I1–I4).
boundary: **Not in this slice:** mapping to canonical items; the review UI.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Generating the shopping list needs structured ingredients. Being rule-based keeps it deterministic and testable.

sections.heading: Owner input
sections.body: None if the items interview is done. Any lines that remain ambiguous get flagged for review, not guessed.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/larder/ingredients/parse.py`
- `src/larder/ingredients/units.py`
- `tests/test_ingredient_parse.py` (table-driven over every line in the fixtures)

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `test_quantities_integers_fractions_mixed_ranges` ("1 1/4", "2/3", "2-3")
2. `test_unit_synonyms` (tbsp/tablespoon, tsp/teaspoons, lb/pound, cup/cups)
3. `test_package_with_size` ("1 can (15 oz) corn, no salt added")
4. `test_optional_flag` ("(optional)")
5. `test_alternatives` ("honey, maple syrup, or agave")
6. `test_parenthetical_and_trailing_notes` ("(modify to taste)", ", chopped")
7. `test_non_food_flag` ("1 small mason jar")
8. `test_unparseable_line_low_confidence_not_exception`
9. `test_all_fixture_lines_parse_with_expected_results` (golden table)

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Tokenize the quantity (unicode fractions too), unit (from the units table), and package-with-size pattern.
2. Remaining text → item text and notes (split on the first comma or parenthetical).
3. Flags: optional, alternatives, non-food (keyword list from ADR 0019).
4. Confidence: start high; lower it for unknown units, missing quantities, or multiple candidates.
5. Pure functions only; no DB.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - Parser tests pass; every line in the sample recipes is either parsed with high confidence or flagged.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Commit only when the owner asks; no AI attribution.
